chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A time will come upon the people when nothing will remain of the Quran except its outline, and nothing of Islam except its name. They will be named by it, but they are the farthest of people from it. Their mosques will be well-built, but they are ruins from guidance. The jurists of that time are the worst of jurists under the shadow of the sky. From them the strife will emerge, and to them it will return.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the decline of the jurists in the era of the Quran's outline?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali and the Prophet, warns of an era of 'formalism' where the Quran remains merely in script and Islam only in name, a concept central to Shia critiques of religious superficiality. It specifically identifies the jurists (fuqaha) of that time as the worst under the sky, linking their spiritual emptiness to the emergence and resolution of major tribulations (fitna). This underscores the Shia emphasis on deep, substantive knowledge over mere ritualistic observance.
